🏙 Almaty

Big Almaty Lake

Turquoise water, glacier views — and absolutely no swimming.
Day 3 · Big Almaty Lake & city afternoon →

A turquoise alpine lake at 2,511 m, set in a bowl of mountains with a glacier above. The colour shifts between deep green and bright turquoise depending on the light. It’s about 40 minutes from central Almaty by car, then a short walk.

⚠️ Vehicle access is the open question: the national park banned cars on the lake road in 2025 (until the first snow, visitors on foot only) and announced restrictions again in April 2026. Check the current rule with the driver before the trip.
Good to know
  • Carry your original passport — the lake sits in a border zone and checks happen.
  • Eco-fee about 650 ₸ per person (2026 tariff).
  • No swimming: it’s Almaty’s drinking-water source. No cafés at the lake — bring snacks and water.
See real photos on Wikimedia ↗

Green Bazaar

A snack crawl, Central Asia style.
Day 2 · Almaty city roam →

Central Asia’s most famous food market: piles of dried fruits, nuts and spices, horse meat and fermented dairy. Come hungry — this is breakfast and lunch.

Good to know
  • Closed on Mondays, which is why it’s on Sunday (Day 2).
  • Try the dried fruit and nuts; bring cash for the stalls.
See real photos on Wikimedia ↗

Ascension (Zenkov) Cathedral & Panfilov Park

A candy-coloured wooden cathedral. No nails!
Day 2 · Almaty city roam →

A colourful wooden Russian Orthodox cathedral, consecrated in 1907 and said to have been built without a single nail — it survived the 1911 earthquake. It stands in Panfilov Park, a pleasant green space with war memorials.

Good to know
  • Free to enter; open daily, roughly 07:00 to early evening (hours vary by source).
  • Dress modestly inside.
See real photos on Wikimedia ↗

Panfilov Street & Zhibek Zholy

Cafés, street art and apple sculptures — wander with a coffee.
Day 2 · Almaty city roam →

A car-free walking zone in the middle of Almaty. Zhibek Zholy was the city’s first stone-paved street (1883), and Panfilov Street was pedestrianised in 2017. Today it’s lined with cafés, street art, apple sculptures and independent shops — the easy, wander-with-a-coffee part of the day.

Good to know
  • Good for lunch: lots of cafés to choose from.
  • Shops open late morning; the street is liveliest in the afternoon and evening.
See real photos on Wikimedia ↗

Arasan Baths

Soviet-era steam: Russian, Finnish and Turkish saunas.
Day 2 · Almaty city roam →

A Soviet-era bathhouse built in 1982 with Russian, Finnish and Turkish saunas. A session of 1.5–2 hours is a very local way to rest tired travel legs.

⚠️ Prices depend on the session length, time and day — weekend sessions cost more than weekdays (about 4,700 ₸, roughly $10, on a weekend). The budget uses $5–10.
Good to know
  • Address: Tulebaev Street 78. Men’s and women’s sections are separate.
  • Bring flip-flops and a towel if you have one; check what’s included when you pay.
See real photos on Wikimedia ↗

Central State Museum + Republic Square

Bronze Age to independence, plus the golden monument on Republic Square.
Day 3 · Big Almaty Lake & city afternoon →

Kazakhstan’s largest museum, with more than 170,000 objects spanning the Bronze Age to independence. Republic Square, a short way away, is the Soviet-scale civic plaza topped by the golden Independence Monument. Allow 1.5–2 hours for the museum. This stop is optional.

⚠️ Sources disagree on the museum’s closed day — several say Monday, others say Tuesday — and Day 3 is a Monday. Check the museum’s own site before planning around it. Entry is listed at about 500 ₸ officially, though one visitor report says 5,000 ₸; the budget uses about $3.
Good to know
  • The museum is in the Samal-1 district (house 44), not directly on Republic Square.
  • Republic Square itself is open-air and free any day.
See real photos on Wikimedia ↗

Almaty Metro stations

Ride a few stops just to see the mosaics — 25 cents a go.
Day 3 · Big Almaty Lake & city afternoon →

Almaty’s metro was begun in the Soviet era and its stations carry mosaics and art. A single ride costs 120 ₸ (about $0.25), so hop a few stations just for the interiors — about 30 minutes in all.

Good to know
  • The fare is from 2024 — check it for 2027.
  • Metro hours are roughly 06:20 to midnight. Pay with a smart card or token.
See real photos on Wikimedia ↗

Soviet architecture walk

Concrete, bas-reliefs and a yurt-shaped circus roof.
Day 3 · Big Almaty Lake & city afternoon →

Almaty is full of Soviet modernism. The Hotel Kazakhstan, the Palace of the Republic and the Arman Cinema, with its bas-relief, stand close together on Dostyk Avenue; the Kazakh State Circus is a separate stop on Abay Avenue. Consider joining a local walking tour.

Good to know
  • Hotel Kazakhstan’s rooftop bar is a popular sunset spot (check it is open).
  • Local walking tours cover the Soviet art — price is not in the budget.
See real photos on Wikimedia ↗

Messa House

A shop that feels like a quiet yurt.
Day 3 · Big Almaty Lake & city afternoon →

A minimalist concept store of about 350 m² that reimagines the Kazakh yurt as a simplified, truncated volume with travertine and limestone. It was designed by UP2DATE Architects and covered by Hospitality Design in July 2026. This stop is optional.

Good to know
  • Check the address and opening hours before going — I could not confirm them.
  • It’s the flagship of the Kazakh womenswear brand Messa.
See real photos on Wikimedia ↗

🏞 Out of town: Charyn, Kolsai & Kaindy

Charyn Canyon — Valley of Castles

Kazakhstan’s mini Grand Canyon.
Day 4 · Charyn Canyon → Saty →

Kazakhstan’s answer to the Grand Canyon. The Valley of Castles has towering red and orange rock pillars carved by about 12 million years of erosion. It’s a walk down into the canyon, not a strenuous hike, and it lies about three hours east of Almaty.

Good to know
  • Allow 1.5–2 hours to walk down to the river and back.
  • Park fee is a few dollars; carry cash. Phone signal is unreliable in the canyon.
  • Bring your passport — it may be checked at the gate.
See real photos on Wikimedia ↗

Saty village

A cosy guesthouse night in the mountains.
Day 4 · Charyn Canyon → Saty →

The base for Kolsai and Kaindy: a small mountain village of guesthouses, about 1.5 hours beyond Charyn. Rooms are simple but clean, with shared facilities and hot water; dinner and breakfast are usually available at the guesthouse.

See real photos on Wikimedia ↗

Kaindy Lake — the sunken forest

A whole forest standing in a lake.
Day 5 · Kaindy & Kolsai → Almaty →

A lake created by a 1911 earthquake-triggered landslide that dammed a mountain valley and submerged a spruce forest. The dead trunks still stand upright in the water, an eerie and beautiful scene. The water is around 5 °C year-round — no swimming.

Good to know
  • Reached from Saty by a short off-road drive in a 4×4, then a walk from the drop-off.
  • Bring your original passport (border zone).
  • Park fees are charged by vehicle and Kolsai charges separately.
See real photos on Wikimedia ↗

Lower Kolsai Lake

One of the “Pearls of the Tien Shan”.
Day 5 · Kaindy & Kolsai → Almaty →

The most accessible of three cascading alpine lakes nicknamed the “Pearls of the Tien Shan”. An easy walk along the western shore gives the best views. We visit on the same day as Kaindy, then drive back to Almaty.

Good to know
  • About 15 minutes’ drive from Saty.
  • Optional boat ride (extra cost). The upper lakes need a long hike and a border-zone permit — not planned.
See real photos on Wikimedia ↗

Bozzhyra Valley & the Fangs

The jaw-dropper. It’s basically Mars.
Day 10 · Mangystau Day 4 — Bozzhyra →

The crown jewel of the trip. Three observation platforms overlook an alien, Mars-like landscape, and a 20-minute hike with about 100 m of climbing leads to the iconic “Fangs” viewpoint.

Good to know
  • The Mangystau tour covers 1,122 km in total (862 km asphalt, 260 km dirt road).
  • Wear sturdy shoes and bring sun protection.

✈️ Getting there

CX681Hong Kong 16:25 → Almaty 20:30
About 7 h 05 m (Almaty is 3 hours behind HK)
CX680Almaty 21:50 → Hong Kong 07:00 next morning
DaysTue · Thu · Sat only. The route starts 9 Jan 2027 and runs through the summer 2027 season.
From JapanAir Astana lists Narita → Almaty (KC172, Tue & Fri, 10:55 → 16:20) and Almaty → Narita (KC171, Mon & Thu, 21:55). Those start 30 Nov 2026 and the Sept 2027 timetable isn’t confirmed yet — check before booking.
Arriving early?You don’t have to land on Day 1. Landing on Day 2 (Sunday) is fine — just be in Almaty for the 09:00 Green Bazaar start. The Day 1 night isn’t counted if you join on Day 2.

🛫 Flying to the desert

  • Almaty ↔ Aktau takes about 3 hours (Air Astana, FlyArystan and SCAT all fly it).
  • Day 6 (Thu): afternoon flight. One option is SCAT DV731, 15:55 → 19:10 — to be confirmed.
  • Day 11 (Tue): morning flight back. Cathay only flies 3 days a week, so choose an early flight and leave a big buffer — missing the connection would be a very long wait! 😅

Timetables for Sept 2027 aren’t out yet, so we’ll confirm when booking.

🌤 Weather & what to pack

  • Almaty in September is lovely: 15–25 °C and dry. The desert is 15–28 °C, and early September can hit the low 30s — later in the month is gentler.
  • Layers (desert nights get chilly), comfy walking shoes, sunscreen, a light windbreaker. No special hiking gear.
  • Kaindy lake is ~5 °C — look, don’t jump in 🥶

🛂 Passport & money

  • Bring your real passport (not a copy) on Days 3, 4 and 5 — Big Almaty Lake, Kolsai and Kaindy are border areas where checks happen.
  • Hong Kong SAR passports get 30 days visa-free. Everyone else: check your own passport.
  • Money is the Kazakhstani tenge (KZT). Cards work well in Almaty; bring cash for villages, park gates and the desert.

🚕 Getting around & chatting

  • Almaty: Yandex Go is like Uber, usually $2–4 across town.
  • Private drivers for the nature days. The desert tour is a private 4×4 trip with Advantour (no camping!).
  • People speak Kazakh and Russian. English is limited outside hotels and tours — download offline Russian in Google Translate.
  • It’s a very safe country for travellers; normal big-city common sense in Almaty.

🤔 Still figuring out

  • The exact dates (Day 1 needs to be a Saturday).
  • Whether cars can drive to Big Almaty Lake in September (see Day 3).
  • Domestic flight times, hotels and the desert tour booking.
  • Whether the Central State Museum is open on your Day 3 (sources disagree on its closed day), and the Messa House address and hours.
  • Prices are from 2025/26 — they may wiggle by 2027.
